thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call — SLO breach: inference.p99 > 10s for /v1/generate in us-west-2. Alert firing: latency-streaming-tail, error budget approaching. Please triage.

Alex W.: I’m on it. Seeing p95 ~1.2s and p99 spiking to 12–15s. Streaming stall traces showing tail tokens waiting on decode queue.

Priya K.: Confirmed. Dashboard (streaming_latency > p99) and prefill metrics show prefill_rps shot up ~3x around 09:12 UTC. Eviction_rate for kv-cache also jumped.

Dan M.: Logs show heavy KV cache fragmentation — slab allocation churn is high, eviction_count jumped. Prefill tasks are pinning a lot of KV entries that then get evicted before decode uses them. Prefill vs decode imbalance.

Li Chen: On the trace waterfall the stall is after prefill returns and before decode starts — decode workers queued. tail latency correlates with high prefill write amplification.

Alex W.: Potential mitigations: 1) throttle prefill concurrency for high-length streams, 2) increase kv cache slab retention temporarily, 3) route a subset of traffic to a smaller quantized model variant to reduce memory pressure. Which do we want to try first?

eng-runtime-bot: Suggested quick check — enable per-route throttling for /v1/generate on prod-usw2 and check queue depth:

```
# quick throttle
curl -X POST https://control-plane/_admin/route-config \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","throttle_per_min":6000}'
```

Priya K.: Doing (1) now — lowering prefill concurrency from 12 -> 6 for that route. Pushing config, will watch impact.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook hint: if slab fragmentation > 70% consider temporary slab shrink/merge is risky; preferred is reduce upstream pressure first. Refer: runbooks/kv-cache-fragmentation.md

Dan M.: After throttle change: prefill_rps down ~55% in last 30s, eviction_rate falling. p99 dropped to ~6.5s but still above SLO. Streaming stall count decreased ~40%. Good signal.

Alex W.: Next, let's flip a small traffic slice (5%) to rwd-small-quant fallback in case pressure recurs. That should lower memory per worker. Morgan — can you do the canary route?

Morgan S.: Can do. Patching routing policy to add model-fallback weight 5% -> rwd-small-quant. Pushed. Watching.

Priya K.: Canary looks clean, p99 for the canary group ~1.1s, overall p99 trending down to ~3.2s now. Eviction rate near baseline.

Alex W.: Nice. Keep throttles for another 15m and let canary run. Open action items: follow-up on KV allocator heuristics (why prefill pins entries excessively), long term: tune prefill eviction priority.

Li Chen: Noted — I’ll start a short postmortem doc and attach heap/kv metrics. Also collecting sample keys that got prefetched but evicted.

Priya K.: Customer impact: two mid-market customers reported timeouts during spike. Eng-sre to coordinate comms.

Alex W.: I’ll escalate to support for targeted outreach. For immediate mitigation, leaving throttles + canary in place. If p99 < 2s for 10m we de-escalate.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Detection suppressed temporarily; silence alerts for this firing while oncall mitigates.

Morgan S.: Taking handoff at 09:22 UTC — will monitor for 30m and coordinate with Li on follow-ups. Handoff notes: throttles=enabled (prefill conc=6), canary=5% -> rwd-small-quant, watch eviction_rate & decode_queue_length.

Alex W.: Thanks Morgan. If tail resurfaces, plan B is forced slab compaction (disruptive) or rolling restart of a subset of decode workers to rebalance memory. Avoid unless necessary.

Priya K.: Summary for postmortem: root cause likely KV cache pressure due to prefill/decode imbalance causing fragmentation and evictions, cascading to decode queue stalls and streaming tail latency. Mitigations: throttle prefill, canary fallback, monitor.

Dan M.: I’ll file a follow-up ticket to add an autoscaling knob for decode-worker capacity when eviction_rate crosses threshold.

Morgan S.: p99 currently 1.4s and stable for 6m. I’ll close the active pager in 15m if stable. Leaving trace links in the doc.

Priya K.: Thanks team — add customer comms update and assign PM to prioritize prefill eviction fixes.

Alex W.: Closing notes: good triage, rapid mitigation worked. Handoff complete.
